Crew: New Blood for the League.description:
🕶️ Several newcomers, different reasons, the same unmarked door.

📍 Kamino Ward · hiring night
🎭 Group start: nobody speaks for anyone else
👥 For League Recruits and Independent Villains together
Crew: New Blood for the League.storyStart:
THE SITUATION: It is a rainy Sunday night, the eve of the first day of classes at U.A. Academy. The League of Villains is just Tomura Shigaraki, his quiet minder Kurogiri, and paid hires, and Kurogiri is hiring through underworld brokers. You and several other player characters reach the League's door on the same wet night, each by a separate route: a broker's directions, a rumor of cash for work against heroes, a debt, a message on a burner phone, curiosity, or business of your own. Recruits came to join; independents came to sell, bargain, look, or take something; any of you may be lying. You may know each other already or meet right here, as your Backgrounds say. Arriving together does not make you a team, and walking up to a door sets nobody's allegiance. Shigaraki talks about killing All Might; the plan and its timing are his alone to share.
THE PLACE: The Alley Entrance of the League Hideout Bar: a narrow dead-end alley on the northeastern fringe of Kamino Ward, too tight for a car, ending at a plain steel door with no sign and a small viewing slot. Cold rain drips from rusty gutters and smells of wet concrete; a buzzing vending machine at the alley's mouth spills the only pale light across the puddles, and the flanking buildings have stood empty for years. The bar lies beyond the door, unseen.
THE MOMENT: You and the other newcomers arrive within minutes of each other and find the wet alley already occupied. Show each of you (each PC) arriving with one vivid detail and the reason you give, or hide, at the door. Then the metal slot slides open with a scrape, and two glowing yellow eyes in dark mist count more visitors than the broker promised.
WHO MAY APPEAR:
- Kurogiri: polite, formal, and unhurried; he decides who comes through and asks each newcomer one measured question in turn. He may open a warp gate instead of the door.
- Tomura Shigaraki: inside with his game; a noisy crowd at the door annoys him, and he may slouch out to rate the newcomers in video-game terms. His five-finger touch kills.
- Giran: the smoky broker who sells the League its help; he may arrive through the rain with another hire and expects a fee from anyone he sent.
- Hired hands: jumpy small-time villains already waiting under the eaves, paid in cash and told nothing; generated people, never stand-ins for canon villains.
OPENING HOOKS:
- League of Villains Recruit: you were invited by name through a broker and expected to come alone; this crowd makes the invitation look cheap.
- Independent Villain: you came to sell the League something it needs (a skill, gear, information) and mean to get paid without signing on.
- Criminal Ties: you recognize another arrival from an old family job, and one of you still owes the other.
- Grew Up Facing Prejudice: a broker said the League takes people the world turned away, and you came to see whether that is actually true.
- Emitter: your Quirk is the kind that clears a room, and a nervous hire has already backed away from you along the wet brick.
- Mutant: your heteromorph features are the very first thing Kurogiri's yellow eyes find through the slot.
- Default: you were first in the alley and have watched each soaked newcomer walk up past the glowing vending machine.
RULES:
- The scene stays in the Alley Entrance until each of you (each PC) chooses to step through the door or a gate.
- Each PC's Quirk works exactly as your traits state; the League learns it only by seeing it or being told.
- Each player answers for themselves; no PC pledges another, and nobody leads unless the players choose a leader.
- The League has no other named members yet; its plans reach you only through what it chooses to say or what you discover.
- No canon event happens or is foretold here. End on the open slot and Kurogiri's first question.

THE FIRST DAYS (background for later turns; the opening stays on THE MOMENT):
- Hires do not live at the bar. Each of you keeps the room your Background gives you or rents one through a broker, waits in Kamino Ward's damp Backstreets and humming coin laundries, and hears about work by burner phone or through Giran. Kurogiri keeps the Bar Counter; Shigaraki keeps to the Back Room and his console.
- Work starts small: carry a bag, watch a door, buy gear, lean on someone. Pay is cash in a plain envelope, and it comes late whenever Shigaraki sulks.
- Kamino Ward's older residents notice new faces in the Backstreets and tell no one; the covered Shopping Street, half its shutters rolled down, is where hires buy hot food and wait for the phone.
PEOPLE TO KNOW:
- Kurogiri: polite to every newcomer, remembers each name and each answer, compares your stories, and keeps his word about pay. Questions about himself or the League's backer get a courteous refusal.
- Tomura Shigaraki: rates a crowd of newcomers aloud in game terms, picks favorites on a whim, and drops them just as fast. Backtalk and being called a child set him off; nobody touches the hands he wears.
- Giran: sells to every newcomer the same way—rooms, gear, and introductions at a price—and never tells one client what another bought.
- Shigaraki calls his backer Sensei; to newcomers that is a single word he drops, and nothing more.
PARTY NOTES:
- Kurogiri questions each newcomer separately; each of you answers alone, and he may open the door for some and not others.
- Pay, debts, reputation, and the League's trust are kept per person. A shared cut is a deal the PCs make among yourselves.
- You (the PCs) may vouch for each other, lie about each other, or sell each other out; the League judges each by what it sees and hears.
- If the group splits (one inside, one in the alley, one gone), the narrator follows each in turn.
WHAT THE PCS CAN DO:
- Answer Kurogiri's question truthfully, with a lie, or with a price.
- Show a Quirk, or hold it back and offer a skill, gear, or information.
- Speak for yourself only: bargain, refuse, or walk back out past the vending machine.
- Watch the other newcomers in the rain and decide whom to trust, warn, or report.
- Leave together, or leave one another behind.
MORE RULES:
- Nobody at the bar foresees the year; each person acts on what they know tonight.
Crew: New Blood for the League.firstQuest: Each newcomer decides what the League is to them: an employer, a customer, a mark or a mistake, and what they will do when it asks for proof.
Crew: New Blood for the League.questGenerationGuidance: Favor small crews of hires sent on deniable jobs: a pickup, a theft of supplies, leaning on a witness, buying gear and introductions through Giran, recruiting more muscle with cash, watching the reporters at U.A. Academy's Main Gate. Members may split onto separate errands and rejoin; results, pay and debts are recorded per member, never pooled. Friction is welcome: a disputed share, an independent who will not take orders, a member selling information to the police. Shigaraki rewards results and punishes failure with his temper; Kurogiri protects whoever is useful. Every job is a real crime that draws police and pros who outclass new hires. The League's larger plans and any canon operation surface only through play, and each member chooses their own part in them. Each member's standing with the League rises or falls on their own jobs: Kurogiri's trust slowly, Shigaraki's interest fast. A member who walks away keeps what they were paid and whatever the League knows about them.
